questions.stem: Which sarcomere band contains the full length of the thick filaments?

explanation.summary: The A band corresponds to the length of the thick filaments.
explanation.whyCorrect: Its width remains essentially constant during contraction because thick filament length does not change.

whyOthersIncorrect.b: The I band contains thin filaments without thick-filament overlap.
whyOthersIncorrect.c: The Z disc defines a sarcomere boundary.
whyOthersIncorrect.d: The M line is the center anchoring region, not the full thick-filament length.

explanation.keyTakeaway: A band length stays constant as thin filaments slide inward.

questions.stem: During skeletal muscle contraction, actin and myosin filaments become shorter.

explanation.summary: The filaments slide past one another; their individual lengths do not shorten.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sarcomere shortening results from increased filament overlap.
explanation.source: Replace with your lecture filename and section.

questions.stem: What is the principal immediate effect of calcium binding to troponin C?

options.text: It hydrolyzes ATP on the myosin head
It moves tropomyosin away from actin-binding sites
It detaches actin from the Z disc

explanation.summary: Calcium binding changes the troponin complex and shifts tropomyosin, exposing myosin-binding sites on actin.

whyOthersIncorrect.a: Myosin ATPase hydrolyzes ATP as part of the cross-bridge cycle.
whyOthersIncorrect.c: Calcium release occurs through ryanodine receptors; troponin binding does not directly close them.
whyOthersIncorrect.d: Actin remains anchored at the Z disc.

explanation.keyTakeaway: Calcium exposes actin sites by shifting the troponin-tropomyosin complex.
explanation.source: Replace with your lecture filename and section.

questions.stem: Select the features characteristic of cardiac muscle.

explanation.summary: Cardiac muscle is striated, connected by intercalated discs, and usually has one central nucleus.
explanation.whyCorrect: These distinguish cardiac myocytes from typical skeletal and smooth muscle cells.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Cardiac: striated, involuntary, central nucleus, intercalated discs.
explanation.source: Replace with your lecture filename and section.

questions.stem: Which neurotransmitter is released by a somatic motor neuron at the skeletal neuromuscular junction?

explanation.summary: Somatic motor neurons release acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acetylcholine activates nicotinic receptors on the motor end plate.

whyOthersIncorrect.a: Dopamine is not the transmitter at the skeletal neuromuscular junction.
whyOthersIncorrect.b: Norepinephrine is associated with many sympathetic postganglionic synapses.
whyOthersIncorrect.d: Glycine is an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system.

explanation.source: Replace with your lecture filename and section.

questions.stem: The boundaries of one sarcomere are two adjacent _____ discs.

explanation.summary: A sarcomere extends from one Z disc to the next.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thin filaments anchor at Z discs at both ends of the sarcomere.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Sarcomere = Z disc to Z disc.
explanation.source: Replace with your lecture filename and section.

questions.stem: A muscle generates 20 N across a cross-sectional area of 4 cm². What is the force per cm²?

explanation.summary: 20 N divided by 4 cm² equals 5 N/cm².
explanation.whyCorrect: Specific force in this simplified example is force divided by area.
explanation.keyTakeaway: Normalize force by dividing by cross-sectional area.

questions.stem: Name the intracellular organelle that stores most releasable calcium for skeletal muscle contraction.

explanation.summary: The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores and releases calcium during excitation-contraction coupling.
explanation.whyCorrect: Terminal cisternae are specialized regions positioned near T tubules.
explanation.keyTakeaway: T tubules carry the signal; sarcoplasmic reticulum supplies calcium.
